requirements.smoothquant-alpha-grid-search: A suitable alpha is obtained by running a grid search on a subset of the Pile validation set, as described in Section 5.1 (Activation smoothing).
requirements.setup-alpha-grid-search-pile-subset: A suitable alpha value is obtained by running a quick grid search on a subset of the Pile validation set, as stated in Section 5.1 (Activation smoothing).

requirements.alpha-too-small-activation-degradation: Figure 10 shows that when migration strength alpha is too small (<0.4) on OPT-175B with LAMBADA, the activations become hard to quantize, leading to model accuracy degradation, consistent with Section 5.5 ablation study.
requirements.alpha-too-large-weight-degradation: Figure 10 shows that when migration strength alpha is too large (>0.6) on OPT-175B with LAMBADA, the weights become hard to quantize, leading to model accuracy degradation, consistent with Section 5.5 ablation study.
requirements.alpha-ablation-too-small-activation-quan: Figure 10 shows that when migration strength alpha is too small (<0.4) on OPT-175B evaluated with LAMBADA, the activations become hard to quantize and model accuracy degrades, consistent with Section 5.5's statement: 'When α is too small (<0.4), the activations are hard to quantize.'
requirements.alpha-ablation-too-large-weight-quantiza: Figure 10 shows that when migration strength alpha is too large (>0.6) on OPT-175B evaluated with LAMBADA, the weights become hard to quantize and model accuracy degrades, consistent with Section 5.5's statement: 'when α is too large (>0.6), the weights will be hard to quantize.'

requirements.alpha-sweet-spot-region: Figure 10 shows that only within the sweet-spot region of alpha between 0.4 and 0.6 on OPT-175B with LAMBADA, both weights and activations achieve small quantization errors and model performance is maintained close to FP16, consistent with Section 5.5 ablation study.
requirements.alpha-ablation-sweet-spot-region-preserv: Figure 10 shows that only when alpha is chosen from the sweet-spot region (0.4-0.6) on OPT-175B evaluated with LAMBADA do both weights and activations achieve small quantization errors, maintaining model performance close to FP16 after quantization, consistent with Section 5.5's statement: 'Only when we choose α from the sweet spot region (0.4-0.6) can we get small quantization errors for both weights and activations, and maintain the model performance after quantization.'

requirements.smoothquant-o1-definition-and-scope: SmoothQuant-O1 is defined and implemented exactly as specified in Table 2: the weight quantization column specifies 'per-tensor' (static, i.e. calibrated offline) and the activation quantization column specifies 'per-token dynamic', representing the highest-accuracy but least computationally efficient of the three SmoothQuant settings (O1, O2, O3), as described in Section 5.1 ('Baselines') and Table 2.
requirements.smoothquant-o3-definition-and-scope: SmoothQuant-O3 is defined and implemented exactly as specified in Table 2: the weight quantization column specifies 'per-tensor' and the activation quantization column specifies 'per-tensor static', representing the most aggressive and most computationally efficient (lowest-latency) of the three SmoothQuant settings (O1, O2, O3), as described in Section 5.1 ('Baselines') and Table 2.
requirements.smoothquant-o1-config-definition: SmoothQuant-O1 has been configured per Table 2 as using per-tensor static weight quantization combined with per-token dynamic activation quantization, representing the highest-accuracy but least-efficient of the three SmoothQuant settings, as stated in Section 5.1 (Baselines) and Table 2.
requirements.smoothquant-o3-config-definition: SmoothQuant-O3 has been configured per Table 2 as using per-tensor weight quantization combined with per-tensor static activation quantization, representing the most aggressive and most efficient (lowest-latency) of the three SmoothQuant settings, as stated in Section 5.1 (Baselines) and Table 2.

requirements.accuracy-mtnlg-530b-negligible-loss-resu: Table 9 has been reproduced, reporting that SmoothQuant enables W8A8 quantization of MT-NLG 530B with negligible accuracy loss on LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA, and WinoGrande, as stated in Section 5.4: 'SmoothQuant enables W8A8 quantization of the 530B model at a negligible accuracy loss.'
requirements.mtnlg-530b-negligible-accuracy-loss-clai: It has been verified that SmoothQuant enables W8A8 quantization of MT-NLG 530B at negligible accuracy loss, as explicitly stated in Section 5.4: 'SmoothQuant enables W8A8 quantization of the 530B model at a negligible accuracy loss,' cross-verified against the INT8 vs FP16 average accuracy values of 73.1% vs 73.1% in the associated accuracy table, and noting individual task differences (LAMBADA +0.6%, HellaSwag -1.7%, PIQA -0.3%, WinoGrande +1.2%) that offset to produce an identical average.
